title: Water-flora foundational growth architecture
scope: Foundational growth architecture of the K4 water-flora kingdom at qualitative strategy grain; usable within shared-setting ecology and adopted downstream story development.
claims: Water flora are individual, non-networked organisms; contact between organisms is ordinary competition or incidental interaction, not kingdom-defining resource sharing.
The kingdom spans submerged, floating-surface, and wet-margin emergent forms.
Each organism has a durable, long-lived anchor gripping bed, stone, or bank; the anchor is the organism's persistent core and holds its stored reserves.
Expendable flexible streamer growth extends from the anchor through the growing season and is shed or sacrificed to ice, flood scouring, and grazing.
Winter and flood survival is anchor-and-reserves survival; regrowth follows the spring freshet.
Kingdom life rhythms are strongly coupled to the seasonal water cycle, and disturbance tolerance is a kingdom-defining pressure met differently by different members.
Mature anchored forms with stiffened streamer bases are a natural candidate for the lake's sturdy egg-substrate plants, which remain formally unassigned.
boundaries: Anchor, streamer, and stiffened base are author-facing functional descriptions, not in-world names or formal taxonomy.
The architecture establishes no Earth kelp, holdfast, reed, waterweed, or other plant homology.
Species, forms, dimensions, proportions, lifespan, growth rates, and silhouettes beyond the theme remain open.
Anchor and streamer anatomy, chemistry, reserve materials, strength, flexibility, and decay remain open.

Streamer shedding is a strategy theme, not a guarantee; severe scouring, ice, drought, disease, grazing, or substrate loss can still kill anchors, and no tolerance threshold or regrowth rate is established.
Energy capture, reproduction, dispersal, seasonal timing mechanisms, and overwintering states remain open.
Whether dedicated floating members exist, and in what form, remains open.

The sturdy egg-substrate plants and flooded vegetation referenced by canon://world/shared-universe-001/ecology/basin-lake-spring-breeding-pulse are not assigned to K4 or to this architecture; candidacy requires its own record.
No water-flora member is established as present, dominant, or absent at any particular location, including the basin lake.
Salinity tolerances, brackish and coastal range, and any marine members remain open.
Grazing relationships, symbioses including any K6 partnership, pests, and diseases remain open.
Earth and mythological inspiration remains author-facing; no living, extinct, or legendary Earth species is transplanted.

Mana patterns remain open; no Mana organ, specialised ability, System progression, spawn point, refill node, guaranteed harvest, reward, Skill, trait payload, or Ancestry Development rule is established.
Water, light or other energy, nutrients, substrate, space, growth time, disturbance, disease, and decay remain binding ecological constraints.
story_implications: Lake and shore scenes can show bare post-freshet anchors, summer streamer beds, grazed and storm-shed drift, and stiffened anchored stands.
Anchor loss, distinct from streamer loss, gives lasting ecological damage a concrete form.
Later nursery, forage, and fishery records gain grounded hooks tied to the seasonal water cycle.
Every species, local presence, assignment, and event requires its own evidence and records.
system_implications: The architecture describes ordinary planetary ecology under CAL0 WLD1.2D and WLD2.1A+D.
No System mechanic, guaranteed harvest, spawn source, refill node, reward, or specialised Mana ability is established.
research_questions: What anchor and streamer anatomy, chemistry, and reserves implement the architecture?
How do members reproduce, disperse, and time their seasonal cycles?
Are the lake's sturdy egg-substrate plants anchored K4 members, and which forms qualify?
What salinity tolerances shape the kingdom's reach toward the brackish coast?
Do dedicated floating members exist, and in what form?
Which grazers, symbioses, pests, and diseases shape water-flora stands?

author_approval.evidence: After the A/B/C architecture cards were presented with A recommended, the Author selected 'A — Anchor-and-streamer' on 2026-08-17.
